RECORDED FOR L9, NO VERDICT. Full text: org/missions/D9/IRPT/IRPT_BCKEND/deliverables/0.7.0_AE_CloudOps~V/the-test-principal-exercised-and-deleted.result.md blob 6f47b38abc24b7ae9002edfd05d06e7b372cfcfb @700bc86ec2, section R60-AC2.
1. PER OUTCOME, THIS ROUND. FWD-1, FWD-2 and FWD-5 are NOT EXERCISED: no session was minted, so no arm made a request. On FWD-1, a partial means 'permitted accounts' is k of the grant set with the remainder disclosed by count; IB-rtf-2's in-process arm read k=21, count=12 of denominator 33 for abby_horton (row W1-S30). Whether that meets the DONE WHEN is the L4 ruling @61627f39f9, graded at L9. FWD-11 is unreachable by a FIRM_ADVISOR principal regardless (not OPAL_GLOBAL), and the roster parameter is a separate, unauthorized act.
2. WHAT IT REVEALED (row IRPT_BCKEND-S86). The token's advisor identity comes from a partner-table binding keyed by e-mail (lib/partner/index.ts:21-37 @4ee8426c72; auth.ts:202-216 @4ee8426c72; jwt.ts:179-185 @4ee8426c72), never from the opal-users-v2 row (db.ts:138-167 @6275297f0e). 0 of 11 partner rows bind abby_horton, so no real login reaches the IRPT scoped routes as abby_horton either. A 49financial principal with no partner row classifies UNKNOWN on the IRPT scoped routes (_scope/resolve.py:193-196 @4ee8426c72) and is admitted by firmId on the older portal routes (lib/partner/index.ts:39-47 @4ee8426c72). That last point is named as an exposure question and was not censused here.
3. REPEATABLE WITHOUT A STANDING ACCOUNT: yes, with TWO keys. A re-cut packet names the opal-users-v2 item and an opal-partner-49financial item for the test e-mail (advisorKey=abby_horton). Each needs its own DeleteItem rollback verified by a consistent read, and the partner key needs its own writer and reader census. After deletion the refresh token dies with the row (refresh sub = PK + createdAt, jwt.ts:220-224 @4ee8426c72), and an issued access token lives at most 15 minutes (jwt.ts:17 @4ee8426c72).
